To obtain the local details of the object, we adopt a progressive training strategy to obtain the semantic information of the object. At different steps, we use different granularity of shuffled versions of the images as input. Then, the classification prediction is performed by fusing the feature representations of different granularities. We obtain the global information of the object by learning jigsaw puzzle visual permutation. Specifically, by introducing the Jigsaw Puzzle Solver module we explore the location information of the different granularity image patches. Recovery of the shuffled version of the image to the original image. Thus, at each step of the network, we supervise the network by complementary relationships between local information of different granularities and global information of the object. Experiments on three standard fine-grained classification datasets (CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, FGCV-Aircraft) show that the performance of our method exceeds that of most methods. The code will be available at https://github.com/Zhao-fan/PPL-Net.

articleTitle: IHFM: An Improved Hierarchical Filtering Method for Multi-source malicious alerts
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Network security situation awareness has recently emerged as a game changer in the security landscape due to its proven potential to help security managers accurately control the system status in real time. However, the exiting method suffer from a large number of misjudgments in the active defense mechanism established based on the alarm data when deal with the huge massive threat logs and event information.Therefore, the method filtering huge warning logs with a fine granularity becomes one of the key problem, which is the basis for the accuracy of the subsequent security situation assessment algorithm. Experiments show that hierarchical filtering performs well for screening of alarm events. In this paper, we propose a five-layer filtering model named IHFM to flexibility filter a large number of alarms in an efficient way. Besides, to further improve the accuracy of model filtering, we propose a concept of the difference in joint performance entropy and introduce the FAHP algorithm to calculate its weight parameters. Lastly, the comparative analysis with experiments in real network environment proves that our proposed method classify and filter malicious events accurately with high flexibility while guaranteeing low false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Urban Fault Detection based on AETA: A Case Study on Line 9 Subway of Shenzhen, China
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: To protect human life and social development, it is necessary to be able to rapidly and accurately identify active faults in urban areas. The traditional methods for detecting active faults, such as geological surveys, artificial seismic exploration, and electromagnetic exploration, are less viable in urban areas with a high concentration of buildings, railway traffic, and underground oil and gas pipelines. Acoustic and Electromagnetic Testing All (AETA) in one system is a system that monitors electromagnetic signals; while this system is typically used to capture abnormal activity prior to the onset of earthquakes, it can also be used as an alternative way to detect geological activity in urban areas. In this study, we propose a novel AETA-based method to determine the location of active faults in urban regions. In order to validate this method, we applied our technique to the Line 9 subway area in Shenzhen. Using AETA data, our model indicated the presence of an activity boundary that has a similar orientation and location to that of a nearby fault. With more measurements, we believe that we can further improve the effectiveness of this new methodology.

articleTitle: Fast and Adaptive Local Consensus Verification for Robust Feature Correspondence
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast and robust feature correspondence verification method based on local consensus. We encode the locality invariance into a continuous probability density function and formulate the problem to be a two posteriori estimation of Bayesian models without accurate transformation estimation. The model can be used without iteration for super-efficiency, and iteratively for SOTA performance. The non-iterative version can directly output the correctness confidence of each match with linearithmic time and linear space complexities. The iterative version requires only 5-10 iterations to update parameters, which can produce SOTA precision or recall. Besides, our model provides remarkable geometry robustness, and is robust to the quality of neighbors even when the simplest spatial knn is used. Numerous experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our method.

articleTitle: Batch Wafer-Identification Recognition Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Wafer identification (ID) is essential for wafer fabrication. Wafer ID can be used to associate production-process data in a manufacture-execution system, which helps product-quality tracing. The related work mainly focuses on single wafer-ID recognition, which requires the wafer to be taken out and placed on a specific platform, resulting in low efficiency. To speed up recognition, we propose a method of batch wafer-ID recognition with a customized optical scheme, which can capture the whole image of a cassette of wafers at once. The proposed scheme does not need to take out the wafers from cassette and avoids the risk of contamination. Based on this scheme, a batch ID recognition algorithm is presented for image preprocessing, undistortion, segmentation, and recognition. We evaluate various image features and classification algorithms for wafer-ID recognition. The experimental results show that a learning-based method like K-Nearest Neighbor using grid feature can achieve high accuracy with high speed, greatly improving the efficiency of wafer-ID recognition.

articleTitle: Lung CT image registration based on end-to-end unsupervised learning
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Medical image registration (MIR) is an important issue of medical image research field, and the purpose of MIR is to establish a spatial correspondence between two medical images. Previous MIR methods based on supervised deep learning usually employ ground-truth or manual landmarks to guide network training. Since ground-truth and manual landmarks are difficult to obtain in practice, the implementation of MIR methods based on supervised deep learning is practically challenging. Currently, most of the MIR methods based on unsupervised deep learning utilize patch-based to learn the local spatial transformation from one image patch to another corresponding patch. Although the patch-based method has satisfactory performance locally, it would generate grid-like artifacts that occur on the edge of the patches during the patch fusion. In this paper, we design a fully convolutional network (FCN), in which the input of the network is a pair of images and the output is the displacement field. The displacement field is applied to warp the moving image to the fixed image through the spatial transformer network (STN) and achieve end-to-end image registration. There is no any supervision information applied in the proposed method. We evaluate the performance of the proposed method using the public DIR-Lab dataset. The average TRE value obtained is 2.03 (1.42), and the registration time is less than one second. The results demonstrate that the method we designed has satisfactory registration capability.

articleTitle: Rate Adaptive Reconciliation Based on Reed-Solomon Codes
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Security of physical layer key generation is based on the randomness and reciprocity of wireless fading channel, which has attracted more and more attention in recent years. This paper proposes a rate adaptive key agreement scheme and utilizes the received signal strength (RSS) of the channel between two wireless devices to generate the key. In conventional information reconciliation process, the bit inconsistency rate is usually eliminated by using the filter method, which increases the possibility of exposing the generated key bit string. Building on the strengths of existing secret key extraction approaches, this paper develops a scheme that uses Reed-Solomon (RS) codes, one of forward error correction channel codes, for information reconciliation. Owing to strong error correction performance of RS codes, the proposed scheme can solve the problem of inconsistent key bit string in the process of channel sensing. At the same time, the composition of RS codes can help the scheme realize rate adaptation well due to the construction principle of error correction code, which can freely control the code rate and achieve the reconciliation method of different key bit string length. Through experiments, we find that when the number of inconsistent key bits is not greater than the maximum error correction number of RS codes, it can well meet the purpose of reconciliation.

articleTitle: CNN based Chromosome Classification Architecture for Combined Dataset
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Karyotyping is the procedure of examing the set of chromosomes from an individual by paring and ordering them. It features chromosome segmentation followed by classification. The resulted images can be used to diagnose genetic abnormalities, but they are usually manually obtained by cytologists, which is time-consuming and labour sensitive. Recently, researches have been carried out on chromosome image classification via Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with significant progress. However, most studies focus on a single dataset for model evaluation, while chromosome images from different datasets are likely to show widely ranged characteristics. This research studies the model performance based on combining two public chromosome datasets, BioImLab and CIR. It proposes a new CNN network constructed by stacking a building block consisting of three convolutional layers followed by one residual layer using the Leaky-ReLU activation. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed model, with 92.97% accuracy, 93.0% recall, and 92.98% precision using the combined dataset, outperforming the traditional ResNet50 and SENet50 networks.

articleTitle: A dense state search method in edge computing environment
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In view of the common edge computing-based cloud-side collaborative environment summary existing search key and authentication key sharing caused by data information leakage, this paper proposes a cryptographic search based on public key searchable encryption in an edge computing environment method, this article uses the public key to search for the characteristics of the encryption algorithm, and allows users to manage the corresponding private key. In the process of retrieval and execution, the security of the system can be effectively ensured through the secret trapdoor. Through the comparison of theoretical algorithms, the searchable encryption scheme in the edge computing environment proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the computing overhead on the user side, and complete the over-complex computing process on the edge server or the central server, which can improve the overall efficiency of encrypted search.

articleTitle: Robust Unsupervised Feature Selection Based on Sparse Reconstruction of Learned Clean Data
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Unsupervised feature selection is an essential task in machine learning. Current methods select representative features under slight noise interference. However, their performance is degraded when the data is grossly corrupted. To fundamentally improve the robustness, we propose a robust unsupervised feature selection method based on the sparse reconstruction of learned clean data(SRCD). In this method, we choose the clean data learned by the low-rank constrain as the reconstruction object. Using the noiseless data, SRCD is then capable of obtaining effective features. To further enhance the interpretability, the projection matrix in the reconstruction term is constrained to column sparse patterns for consistent feature selection. Experiment results based on the benchmark and noisy data confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Indoor Scene Recognition by Fusing Map-Level and Frame-Level Decisions with CRF
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: It’s a fundamental function for a service robot to recognize the type of its ambient scene. However, indoor service robots usually can’t get enough information of the scene with a single frame due to the limited field of view. Furthermore, lack of information may cause the robot to make incorrect judgments about the category of the current scene. To address this problem, we proposed a scene recognition model, based on conditional random field, which integrated the map-level and frame-level scene recognition results. By fusing the two different scene recognition results, the model could more fully utilize the information in the scene to obtain the final scene recognition result. The model first used a dense 3D semantic mapping model SemanticFusion to build a 3D semantic map based on the images collected by the robot, and then used the spatial relationship between objects existing in the semantic map to perform a map-level scene recognition. Meanwhile, key frames were used to get frame-level scene recognition results with neural network. Finally, conditional random field was adopted to fuse map-level and frame-level scene recognition results. Scene recognition based on 3D semantic map and scene recognition based on conditional random field were tested on Stanford 3D dataset and NYU V2 dataset respectively. The experimental results show that our scene recognition model which integrates map-level and frame-level decisions outperform both the map-level scene recognition model and the frame-level scene recognition model. In addition, the robot can use the 3D semantic map with scene category annotation generated in this paper to accomplish its task better.

articleTitle: Design of scenario experiment framework for security protocol
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: At present, in the field of security protocol research and design, most researches lack the actual scene verification link, resulting in that the designed protocol is reliable only under ideal conditions but not necessarily safe in practical application. In the real scene, security protocols face the constraints of equipment, resources and environment, so they often can not meet the functional performance requirements of the actual system, and can not give full play to the protection efficiency of data and assets. In order to solve this problem, a scenario experiment framework for security protocol is proposed. Based on the idea of design pattern, the core class framework is designed and the prototype system is implemented. Protocol researchers can use this framework to quickly and flexibly build a protocol experimental environment matching with real application scenarios, which complements with formal analysis tools, so as to lay a solid foundation for promoting the rapid application of new security protocols.

articleTitle: Rotational Doppler Extraction of Multi-scattering-point Target Using Vortex Electromagnetic Wave with Two Opposite OAM Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Rotational Doppler shift in vortex electromagnetic (EM) wave radar system can provide more detailed features of rotating objects, especially the features which is perpendicular to the radar line of sight (LOS) direction. In this paper, we investigate the extraction of rotational Doppler shift of multi-scattering-point target using vortex EM wave with opposite orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes (topological charges). Firstly, a multi-scattering-point target rotational Doppler model is established, and its characteristics in the time-frequency (TF) domain are studied by signal simulation. Then, a method is proposed for extracting the rotational Doppler shift of the multi-scattering-point target based on the vortex EM wave with opposite OAM modes. Theoretical and electromagnetic simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which is of great advantage to acquire more information of rotating target through vortex-EM-wave-based radar.
